profile.summary: GENA-LM is a family of transformer DNA language models for reading long genomic sequences, up to 36,000 base pairs in its sparse-attention versions. It takes DNA split into variable-length tokens and returns sequence representations that are fine-tuned for tasks such as promoter, splice site, enhancer and chromatin profile prediction. Most models were trained on the human T2T genome, and species-specific and multispecies models also exist.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract, Materials and methods (Sequence tokenization); README_previous_generation.md: Pre-trained models, Downstream tasks

summary_quotes.text: a suite of transformer-based foundational DNA language models capable of handling input lengths up to 36 000 base pairs

DNA sequences are tokenized using a BPE algorithm before being processed through transformer layers, which generate representations of the input sequences that are suitable for downstream applications.
Downstream tasks for model evaluation encompass the prediction of promoter and enhancer activity, splicing sites, chromatin profiles, and polyadenylation site strength.
we have developed and released species-specific models for yeast, Arabidopsis and Drosophila, as well as a multispecies model

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GENA-LM models are BERT-style transformer encoders trained as masked language models. DNA is first split by a Byte-Pair Encoding tokenizer with a dictionary of 32 000 tokens, so one token covers several bases; the paper reports a median token length of 9 bp. BERT models use pre-layer normalisation. Three models reach 4096 tokens (about 36,000 bp): two use DeepSpeed sparse attention with rotary position embeddings, and bigbird-base-t2t uses the Hugging Face BigBird implementation. The paper also describes fine-tuning with a recurrent memory mechanism to process even longer segments.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository table lists eight pretrained checkpoints: five BERT models of 512 tokens (4500 bp) and three BigBird-style models of 4096 tokens (36000 bp). They differ in depth (12 or 24 layers), in the data used for the tokenizer and for training (T2T only, T2T with 1000 Genomes SNPs, or with multispecies data), and in which chromosomes were held out. The paper also names yeast, fly and Arabidopsis models. Fine-tuned checkpoints for promoters and splice sites are kept as branches of the Hugging Face repositories. A result should name the checkpoint, the branch if any, and the Hugging Face revision; this page read gena-lm-bert-base-t2t at revision 4f1352bd. The developers have since released a successor family, modernGENA, in the same repository.

run_guide.summary: Load the pretrained gena-lm-bert-base-t2t checkpoint from Hugging Face with the transformers library.
prerequisites: Python with the transformers library. The sources read give no install command or version for this route.
The sparse-attention checkpoints (bigbird-base-sparse, bigbird-base-sparse-t2t) additionally need FP16, DeepSpeed and a GPU of compute capability 7 or above; this guide does not cover them.
Code is MIT licensed. The model card read declares no weights licence.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/AIRI-Institute/GENA_LM.git
cd GENA_LM
git checkout --detach ed71502f71538ea1e28485381ac94fcae7211818
steps.explanation: The README's clone command. The cd and checkout lines are added to pin the commit this page was written from. The clone is needed only for the repository's own model classes; the next step loads code from Hugging Face.

quotes.text: git clone https://github.com/AIRI-Institute/GENA_LM.git

steps.title: Load the pretrained model
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('AIRI-Institute/gena-lm-bert-base-t2t')
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('AIRI-Institute/gena-lm-bert-base-t2t', trust_remote_code=True)
PY
steps.explanation: The README snippet for masked language modelling, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the tokenizer, the weights and the model code from Hugging Face.
